eyebrow: INDUSTRIES · PHARMACEUTICAL · BIOTECHNOLOGY · MEDICAL DEVICES · CDMO
headline: Your products set the water grade. Your regulator sets the evidence. Start from both.
lead: Pharmacopoeia limits do not change by industry: Purified Water (PW) and Water for Injection (WFI) are judged at USP <645> 1.3 µS/cm at 25 °C and 500 ppb total organic carbon (TOC), and WFI at < 0.25 EU/mL endotoxin under USP <85>. What changes is where the water touches your product and who reads the record: Health Canada under GUI-0001 and GUI-0119 for drugs, an MDSAP auditor under ISO 13485 for devices, and every client's quality unit at a contract manufacturer. Choose your industry to see the grades, limits, inspectors and documents for your plant, then the systems that hold them at the point of use.

blocks.intro: Each industry page carries the grade each process step needs, the limits you release against, what each inspector reads and the documents we hand over. Each ends in a scope review written for that buyer.

items.d: PW for oral solids, liquids and creams; WFI and pure steam for parenterals. Written to Health Canada GUI-0001 and GUI-0119, 21 CFR Part 211 and Ph. Eur., including natural health products under GUI-0158.

WFI in volume for media, buffers and clean-in-place (CIP) final rinse, and pure steam for sterilize-in-place (SIP), held to < 0.25 EU/mL at the furthest outlet at peak draw and phased from clinical to commercial scale.

Final rinse water with limits worked back from your device: USP <161> 20.0 EU per device, 2.15 EU for cerebrospinal fluid contact, and the ISO 11737-1 bioburden behind your sterilization dose. Documented for ISO 13485, MDSAP and FDA QMSR.

One system audited by every client and every regulator they ship to: built to the stricter of USP and Ph. Eur. on each attribute, with redundancy priced against downtime and a client audit pack with trend data under 21 CFR Part 11.

blocks.h: The same limits, applied where the water touches your product
blocks.body: A tablet maker, a biologics plant and an implant maker can all release water against USP <645> and <643>. They differ in which step uses which grade, how much they draw at peak and which record the auditor opens first. We design around those three, factory acceptance test (FAT) each system before it ships and hand over the installation and operational qualification (IQ/OQ) protocols with it.

blocks.h: Questions buyers ask before choosing a page

items.q: We make more than one kind of product. Which page do we read?
items.a: The one for your strictest product. A plant making oral solids and one sterile line reads the sterile rows of the pharmaceutical page; a device maker with a drug-device combination product also reads the pharmaceutical page for the drug part. A contract manufacturer reads the CDMO page, which covers designing to the stricter of USP and Ph. Eur. on each attribute.

items.q: Do the limits change with the industry?
items.a: No. USP <645>, <643> and <85>, and the Ph. Eur. monographs, set the same limits for PW and WFI whoever uses them. What changes is which grade each step needs, the device limits a device maker works back from, and how the record is audited. Microbial alert and action levels are yours to set; USP <1231> gives guidance of 100 CFU/mL for PW and 10 CFU/100 mL for WFI.

items.q: Our product is not in these four industries. Can you still help?
items.a: If it is a drug, including a natural health product, the pharmaceutical page covers it. For hospital reprocessing, laboratory or industrial water, see the adjacent uses above and send the standard you work to. We will tell you plainly whether it is in our scope.
